newsitem.title: JAPAN: Iraq changes oil contract term for Mitsubishi Corp.
newsitem.headline: Iraq changes oil contract term for Mitsubishi Corp.

text.p: Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) has changed the terms of its oil sales contract with Mitsubishi Corp, reducing the volume to 20,000 barrels per day and extending the period to six months, industry sources said on Monday.
The contract, initially for 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) over three months, was changed to 20,000 bpd over six months at SOMO's request, they said.
"SOMO made the request (late last year)...and there was no room for negotiations," one trader said.
He added the change was final.
Mitsubishi officials involved in the contract could not be immediately reached for comment.
Sources said that in response, Mitsubishi asked that it be allowed to lift another 40,000 bpd over April to June.
SOMO has not yet responded to the request, the sources said.
The industry sources said about six other companies had been told of similar changes to their initial contracts.
The names of the companies were not available, however.
SOMO reportedly told Mitsubishi that the United Nations had warned Baghdad about the volume that it had contracted.
As of January 3, 21 companies had agreed to buy a total of 551,000 bpd of crude oil from Iraq. Contract terms are either for three or six months.
The sources said it would probably take a long time for Iraq to respond to Mitsubishi's request for extra crude oil volumes.
Mitsubishi is the only Japanese company to have reached an agreement to purchase oil from Iraq under a U.N. oil-for-food deal.
Under the current U.N. oil-for-food deal, Iraq can ship only $2 billion worth of crude oil over six months to raise money to buy humanitarian relief supplies for its citizens.
